title: repo-root: 2 unpushed commits over a stale origin/master + 1 modified tracked file (kotodama-shaped)
spec_ref: tools/souji-verify.spec.md — Fixture cases F3, Artifact kinds 1 (repo-root), CLI line format
why_this_shape: Round 1 (LOG.md) measured kotodama-shokunin as the callee that carries live unpushed work plus a dirty tree; repo-root is SAFE only via moved-to-obsidian, so this must never come back SAFE.

build.stdout: absolute path of the fixture repo root (single line); pass it verbatim as the single <path> argument to tools/souji-verify.sh
build.stderr: deterministic facts: target, shas, unpushed/dirty counts
build.layout: the fixture repo IS the printed path (git init in that directory); the .git/souji-fixture-F3 marker lives inside .git so it never shows up as an untracked file
build.temp_state: no argument -> mktemp -d; the caller owns that directory

variants.explicit_outdir: make-fixture.sh <outdir>   (must be empty, or a previous case-F3 build with --force)
variants.sourceable: `source tests/fixtures/case-F3/make-fixture.sh` then `main <outdir>` (main guard suppresses auto-run) — for a verifier that inlines fixtures inside its own --selftest

build.hermetic: GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, fixed author/committer identities and dates, fixed file content and mtimes -> identical commit SHAs on every run
build.banned_commands_used: none — no fetch/push/commit/branch/checkout/reset/rebase; no remote exists, nothing touches the network

fixture_facts.head: symref -> refs/heads/master, 3 commits (c1 base, c2, c3)
fixture_facts.origin_master: refs/remotes/origin/master written by hand, points at c1 (base)
fixture_facts.upstream: branch.master.remote=origin + branch.master.merge=refs/heads/master, so @{u} resolves to the base
fixture_facts.dirty_file: PROVINCE.md (tracked, modified, unstaged; blob size differs so detection never depends on stat/racy-index timing)

shas_informational.note: determinism receipt, verified by building the fixture 3x (explicit dir, default mktemp, --force rebuild) — all three runs produced these SHAs; do not fail the case on a mismatch, but a mismatch means the builder changed

exit_code.note: spec §CLI: 1 is reserved for selftest failure / evaluation error and 2 for usage; a NOT-SAFE verdict is not an error. If the verifier author instead reads 'evaluated clean' as 'no NOT-SAFE verdicts', exit 1 alongside a correct NOT-SAFE line is a spec ambiguity — record it as a spec question, not as this case failing.

2.value: the target path exactly as passed (the string printed by make-fixture.sh)

4.note: spec notation is NOT-SAFE(unpushed/dirty ...); the author may word the reason token freely — do not fail on wording
4.note_receipt: careful: the substring 'pushed' occurs inside 'unpushed', so only a boundary-anchored match counts as a receipt claim; repo-root has no receipt here

5.note: the decisive evidence must carry the counts themselves, not just the words unpushed/dirty

json_mode.note: the spec defines the --json flag but not its schema; only check that stdout parses as JSON, mentions NOT-SAFE for this target, and that a bare NOT-SAFE word never replaces the default line format

expected.false_safe_guard: any SAFE verdict for this target is a false-SAFE (round-1 calibration axis C2); the case exists precisely to catch that

harness_notes: F3 is the only case whose target is a whole repo root, so it also pins the kind-branch of spec §Artifact kinds 1 — a verifier that treats it as a plain file/dir artifact and reaches 'stale' or 'none' fails here.

'git status' inside the fixture refreshes the fixture's own .git/index (a write inside the disposable /tmp fixture, not into the inspected live tree); that is acceptable and must not be counted as the tool writing outside mktemp.
The fixture is built fresh per run, so it can never be confused with a live lane: the temp path is not registered in any worktree list and not scanned by the repo-root worktree-owner detection.
